newsitem.title: USA: Intel Q1 gross margin rose to 64 percent.
newsitem.headline: Intel Q1 gross margin rose to 64 percent.

text.p: SANTA CLARA, Calif., April 14 (Reuter) Intel Corp. said first quarter 1997 gross margins were 64 percent, up from the strong 63 percent it reported in the final quarter of 1996 and from 48 percent in the year-ago first quarter.
Intel attributed the strong gross margins in the first quarter of 1997 to a more favorable product mix.
The company said, in a statement released with its quarterly earnings report, that it expects gross margin in the second quarter "to be flat to slightly down from 64 percent in the first quarter."
Introduction of new products, which tend to enter at higher price points, and strong manufacturing performance helped the Intel's product mix during the first quarter, the company said.

Intel said "excellent manufacturing performance" had allowed the company to rapidly gear up production of its new, more powerful Pentium processor with its MMX technology, introduced early in the quarter.

"The company is currently adding capacity and transitioning existing capacity both to meet the additional manufacturing requirements of the Pentium with MMX technology, Pentium Pro and Pentium II processors...," it said.

The company said that it still believes that over the long-term the gross margin percentage will be 50 percent plus or minus a few points. with the gross margin percentage varying depending on product mixes.

First quarter 1997 total expenses, including research and development, marketing, general and adminstration costs, rose 39 percent to $1.3 billion from $918 million due primarily to higher levels of research and development, advertising and revenue-dependent expences.
Expenses were 20 percent of revenues in the first quarter, the same percentage as they had been in the first quarter of 1996.
